To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cAMP response element in the TBM promoter is involved in transcriptional activation in response to c-AMP.
The TBM 5'-flank region contains CREs with an octamer like motif.
The tracheobronchi al mucin gene contains cAMP-responsive elements (CREs), and CREs provide a nuclear protein-binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the transcription factors that regulate the mucin gene in normal and disease states.
the identification of cis-acting elements that regulate mucin gene transcription and the identification of trans-acting factors that interact with these elements.
the identification of cis and trans elements involved in the regulation of mucin expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TBM CRE is responsive to cAMP and may be involved in the transcriptional upregulation of the TBM in response to ciliary beat frequency (CBF) and other stimuli.
the TBM CRE is a cis-acting DNA element that mediates cAMP induction of gene transcription.
CREs are important for cAMP-mediated regulation of the TBM 5'-flaking region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TBM CRE is a cAMP-responsive cis-acting element that mediates cAMP-induced transcription of TBM in human tracheobronchi al epithelial cells.
the TBM gene contains cAMP-responsive CREs that are functional in HBE1 cells.
the TBM gene is regulated by CREs, and CREB may play a key role in the transcriptional regulation of the TBM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CREs in the TBM promoter region are functional and can mediate induction in response to c AMP in HBE1 cells.
cAMP is a positive modulator for TBM gene expression in HBE1 cells.
the TBM gene is a direct target of CREB.
